hints: Focus on the class of each alcohol, primary, secondary or tertiary, because that controls how it behaves with acidified dichromate(VI).
Recall that butan-2-ol has its OH on a middle carbon with two alkyl groups, so it is a secondary alcohol.
Compare how many stages a primary alcohol can be oxidised through versus a secondary alcohol to see which gives just a single product.
walkthrough:
**Classify each alcohol**

First, look at the carbon carrying the OH group. Count how many other carbons it is joined to to decide primary, secondary or tertiary.

$\text{butan-1-ol: primary}$, $\text{butan-2-ol: secondary}$, $\text{2-methylpropan-1-ol: primary}$, $\text{2-methylpropan-2-ol: tertiary}$

**Recall the oxidation rules**

Primary alcohols oxidise in two stages, secondary in one stage, tertiary resist oxidation under these mild conditions.

$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone only}$$
$$\text{tertiary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$

**Apply to this question**

Both primary alcohols can give two different products depending on conditions. The tertiary alcohol gives no product at all.

Only the secondary alcohol, butan-2-ol, stops at one stable product, butan-2-one, which cannot be oxidised further.

options.A: Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. It oxidises first to butanal and then to butanoic acid, so two possible oxidation products, not one.
options.B: Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It oxidises in one step only to the ketone butan-2-one, which resists further oxidation, so exactly one possible product.
options.C: 2-methylpropan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$. Like all primary alcohols it gives two products, 2-methylpropanal then 2-methylpropanoic acid.
options.D: 2-methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$. It has no hydrogen on the carbon with the OH, so it is not oxidised by warm dilute acidified dichromate(VI) and gives zero products.
